brief: What a decade of client work teaches about being paid properly

slots.eyebrow: Ten years, roughly two hundred projects
slots.subtitle: Six lessons about getting paid for it, each one learned the expensive way and none of them about craft.
slots.word1Sub: Every argument starts as an assumption nobody wrote down
slots.word2Sub: The number is usually fine; the silence after it is not
slots.word3Sub: What you agree in advance you never have to negotiate

slots.body: Every unbilled hour started life as a shared assumption that neither side said out loud. The exclusions protect the relationship far more than the inclusions do, because they are the only part anyone reads twice.
slots.bullet2: A rate agreed for out-of-scope work
slots.bullet3: An expiry on the quote itself

slots.body: The pause after a price feels far longer to the person who said it. Filling that silence is how a rate gets discounted before anyone has objected to it, and it is entirely self-inflicted.
Asking for money before starting is standard everywhere except in the head of somebody who has never asked. It also removes, before any work happens, the clients who were never going to pay.
slots.bullet3: Late terms stated once, never enforced

slots.body: Almost every relationship that survived a serious mistake survived because somebody said it first. The cost of a problem roughly doubles for every day it goes unmentioned, and the client always finds out.
slots.bullet2: Bring the fix, not the apology

slots.body: Your real rate is whatever your last satisfied client tells somebody you are worth. Nothing on a portfolio moves that number, which is why the last project sets the price of the next one.
slots.bullet2: Recommend others when you are wrong for it
slots.bullet3: Stay in touch after the invoice clears

slots.body: Positioning raises what people will pay for a given standard. It does not raise the standard, and a client who feels overcharged does not come back and does not refer you, which removes the only channel that mattered.
slots.bullet1: The rate has to be earned first
slots.bullet2: The market corrects within two projects
slots.bullet3: Raise it until you feel resistance

slots.eyebrow: On the next proposal, not the current one
slots.body: Not on the clients you have, and not by an amount you would need to justify. On the next one, and only after the exclusions are written down.
slots.preLine: Write down what you will not do, name the number once, and let the silence belong to them.
slots.signoff: The resistance is the actual price
